item.title: Lecture 3
item.description: As usual, consider \alpha:I\mapsto \mathbb{R}^3 p.a.l. with k>0, s\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}T(s)\\ N(s)\\ B(s)\end{pmatrix}\in \mathbb{R}^3. Then, \begin{pmatrix}T'(s)\\ N'(s)\\ B'(s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}k(s)N(S)\\ -k(s)T(s)-\tau(s)B(s)\\ \tau(s)N(s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}O_3 & k(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3\\ -k(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3 & -\tau(s)\mathrm{I}_3\\ O_3 & \tau(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}T(s)\\ N(s)\\ B(s)\end{pmatrix} Theorem 1(Fundamental theorem of the local theory of curves).
